items.title: Carney wraps meetings on security, trade with European leaders in Ireland
items.summary_auto: Prime Minister Mark Carney heard from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Thursday about the state of negotiations with Russia as the two discussed continental security with European leaders.

items.title: Russian federation head Tretiak says it will seek compensation if barred from world juniors in Alberta
items.summary_auto: Russian hockey federation president Vladislav Tretiak is threatening to seek compensation from Canada and push for the relocation or cancellation of next month's world junior championship in Alberta if Russia is barred from competing.

items.title: Industry minister terminates resolution talks with Stellantis over Brampton auto plant sale
items.summary_auto: Industry Minister Mélanie Joly has written the CEO of Stellantis Canada saying the government is terminating a resolution process and notifying the automaker that it is in default of a 2022 funding agreement after the company announced its intentions to sell its Brampton, Ont., plant to an armoured vehicle manufacturer.

items.title: Will U.S. travel pick up after midterm 'blue wave'? Not so fast, say these Canadians
items.summary_auto: Travel from Canada to the U.S. dropped amid President Donald Trump's threats and trade war. While many Canadians view the Democratic Party's midterm election victory as an 'encouraging' sign, they say it's too soon to visit the U.S. again amid continued distrust.

items.title: A PAL Airlines flight lost a wheel 2 weeks ago. It's happened again — to the same plane
items.summary_auto: Less than two weeks after a PAL Airlines flight lost a wheel, the airline has confirmed the same plane lost another one Thursday. Flight 411 was bound for Deer Lake, Newfoundland and Labrador, but instead landed in St. John's.

items.title: Hegseth awards medal to Arlington soldier who scolded his group on decorum
items.summary_auto: U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth has given a top award to the service member who scolded him and his staff at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier following a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery.

items.title: Report of children confined in locker at Quebec school draws minister's condemnation
items.summary_auto: Students at a primary school were allegedly placed in a metal locker as a disciplinary measure. The Education Ministry is in touch with the investigating authorities to better understand what took place.

items.title: CBC announces Hockey Night in Canada broadcast team for PWHL season
items.summary_auto: In forming its broadcast team for the return of Hockey Night in Canada with Professional Women’s Hockey League coverage, CBC Sports has turned to broadcasters, journalists, and former players.

items.title: The U.S. is now urging middle-aged men to routinely screen for prostate cancer. What about Canada?
items.summary_auto: Middle-aged men should undergo regular screening for prostate cancer, the American Cancer Society said Thursday in a major change to U.S. guidelines. It comes a month after the Canadian Cancer Society urged a new national advisory body to update its prostate cancer guidelines.

items.title: NCC mulling refrigerating downtown end of Rideau Canal
items.summary_auto: The CEO of the National Capital Commission (NCC) says the Crown corporation is seriously mulling artificially freezing the northern end of the Rideau Canal to make skating conditions more reliable in the winter.

items.title: Frankie Muniz, race-car driver and actor, released from hospital after crash
items.summary_auto: Actor and race-car driver Frankie Muniz has been released from a hospital following a practice-lap crash at Florida's Daytona International Speedway. The 40-year-old star of Malcolm in the Middle was practising for a Veterans Day benefit race set for Wednesday night.

items.title: U.S. envoys head to Dublin to talk to Zelenskyy, after prior sitdown with Putin
items.summary_auto: U.S. envoys met Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin before heading to Ireland for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Washington sought new momentum for its peace efforts.

items.title: Carney aware of 'some aspects' of Stellantis auto plant sale, but says company still broke deal
items.summary_auto: Prime Minister Mark Carney says he had been informed of "some aspects" of Stellantis's plan to sell an idled Brampton, Ont., auto plant to Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc., before the deal was announced.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after affair raises national security concerns
items.summary_auto: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy raised national security concerns. It comes after reporting late on Wednesday that he had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reports to him.

items.title: Anthropic IPO to test the first 'pure play' AI stock in a choppy market
items.summary_auto: American AI giant Anthropic's expected debut on the Nasdaq has one money manager recalling the dot-com bubble of the 2000s.

items.title: Yella Beezy found guilty in murder-for-hire of fellow Dallas rapper
items.summary_auto: Rapper Yella Beezy was found guilty on Wednesday of hiring the gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3 in a brazen daylight attack on a busy Dallas interstate in 2020.

items.title: Lockdowns are happening at Whitehorse jail for wrong reasons, advocates say
items.summary_auto: Inmates at Whitehorse Correctional Centre faced unscheduled lockdowns almost every second day this year, adding up to hundreds of additional hours confined to their cells. Lawyers say that affects mental health, access to programming and court proceedings.

items.title: How a charity is trying to remove 'countless' images posted by Canada's most prolific voyeur
items.summary_auto: Yin Yeung Derek Chan was sent to prison earlier this year, but some of the "countless" videos and photos he took of 652 women and girls in Greater Victoria continue to spread online.

items.title: Ontario's moose population is in decline, and the province is trying to figure out why
items.summary_auto: The Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry says strong predation numbers of wolves and black bears could be a major factor in moose decline while a conservationist says rising temperatures are putting stress on the large mammals.

items.title: Canada has the opportunity to become a global LNG leader, new report says
items.summary_auto: Canada’s only liquified natural gas facility began operating last year, yet the country has an opportunity to scale up that industry and become one of the top natural gas exporters in the world, according to a new report.

items.title: Mice, pigeon infestations at Halifax-area hospitals lead to soaring pest-control costs
items.summary_auto: CBC News has learned that several Halifax-area hospitals have been dealing with soaring costs to deal with mice and pigeon infestations. Nova Scotia Health says it could take years to rid its facilities of the mice issue.

items.title: Ontario's moose population is in decline, scientists have different theories on the reasons why
items.summary_auto: The Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry says strong predation numbers of wolves and black bears could be a major factor in moose decline while a conservationist says rising temperatures are putting stress on the large mammals.

items.title: Indonesia's vice-president resigns after academic credentials questioned
items.summary_auto: The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents Gibran Rakabuming Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements.

items.title: Missing teen found alive after 6 days in the Australian woodlands
items.summary_auto: A 17-year-old boy with autism was found alive Thursday after six days lost in eastern Australian woodlands.

items.title: Israeli strike on a Gaza hospital kills 6 people, including surgeon, health authorities say
items.summary_auto: An Israeli airstrike on southern Gaza's main hospital overnight killed at least six Palestinians, including a surgeon and a teenage boy, medics said, the latest Israeli attack to undermine a year-old ceasefire in the war-shattered territory.

items.title: LinkedIn, Monster take down over 1,000 fake job postings after CBC investigation
items.summary_auto: More than 1,500 misleading job postings on LinkedIn and Monster were actually connected to a multi-level marketing company, a CBC News visual investigation has found.

items.title: I studied silence in Ukraine, but moving to Montreal made me truly understand it
items.summary_auto: When Anna Lyhina moved from Ukraine to Quebec, she realized immigration can produce its own form of silence — not because anyone forbade her to speak. Learning a new language was about becoming herself again.

items.title: Montreal tenants without hot water, electricity during heated dispute over renovations
items.summary_auto: A group of private investors bought the units in 2024 under the banner Norgate Québec Inc. The Comité logement Saint-Laurent says many of the units are occupied by immigrants and recent newcomers to Quebec.

items.title: Severe stomach bug hits Montreal’s homeless population, shelter workers raise alarm
items.summary_auto: A severe stomach bug has spread through Montreal's homeless population, raising concern among shelter workers who say not enough is being done to contain it.

items.title: Border control pilot launched to stem drug smuggling into 5 First Nations in northern Ontario
items.summary_auto: A new border control pilot program aims to prevent drug and alcohol smuggling into five First Nation communities in northern Ontario, with some pointing to the Toronto area as a source of drugs entering the communities. The program, led by the largest Indigenous police force in Canada, was launched as Nishnawbe Aski Nation is in a state of emergency over drug trafficking and related violence.

items.title: American Airlines resumes flights to Haiti, providing a vital route into the country
items.summary_auto: The U.S. airline has begun flying into northern Haiti on a daily basis, providing a vital route into the country at a time when Americans have few options to get there as the U.S. government advises people to avoid all travel to the Caribbean nation due to security concerns.

items.title: How China gets around the U.S. ban on Nvidia chips
items.summary_auto: The revelation that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a former executive of a Singapore-based company has raised concerns about China's ability to acquire top-tier microchips restricted to the country.

items.title: Hegseth, wife and aides spark scolding from guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
items.summary_auto: A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery issued a verbal reprimand to a group of advisers and staffers with U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth following a Veterans Day ceremony.

items.title: Series of storms leaves B.C. woman with tree stuck on her house for days
items.summary_auto: A B.C. woman who saw a tree fall onto her house last Friday says it'll have to remain in place as high winds continue to batter the province.

items.title: Death toll climbs to 8 in Brooklyn building collapse
items.summary_auto: Eight people have died after a three-storey building in Brooklyn collapsed at the edge of a construction site, New York City's mayor said Thursday, as firefighters kept digging through the rubble to find others who may be trapped beneath the wreckage.

items.title: Ottawa had been aware of Stellantis-Roshel talks for months, source says
items.summary_auto: The federal government had been made aware for months about the possibility that Stellantis would sell its Brampton, Ont., assembly plant to a light armoured vehicle manufacturer, a source has told CBC News.

items.title: Mississippi's Scott Colom secures Senate seat in another midterm win for Democrats
items.summary_auto: Mississippi Democrat Scott Colom will be the state's first Black senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction era. Colom's victory also offers Democrats an unexpected boost in their effort to win control of the U.S. Senate.

items.title: Martin Luther King Jr.'s handwritten draft of 'I Have a Dream' speech found in desk drawer
items.summary_auto: The day Martin Luther King Jr. stood on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial and delivered his iconic "I Have A Dream" speech is forever etched in the annals of history. But the night before — when the U.S. civil rights leader stayed up alone in his hotel room scribbling his now-famous words on a yellow notepad — was a moment lost to time. Until now.

items.title: Heritage Minute filmed in Wainwright honours fallen Canadian soldier
items.summary_auto: Capt. Jon Snyder received a Star of Military Valour for his leadership and bravery when his team was attacked in Afghanistan in 2008. The Heritage Minute was filmed at CFB Wainwright and the surrounding area over the summer.

items.title: Canadian government says Russian players with visas will still be barred from WJC
items.summary_auto: The federal government says Russian hockey players will not be permitted to compete at next month's world junior championship in Alberta, even if they already hold valid Canadian visas.

items.title: Canada says Russian hockey players with visas will still be barred from world junior championship
items.summary_auto: The federal government says Russian hockey players will not be permitted to compete at next month's world junior championship in Alberta, even if they already hold valid Canadian visas.

items.title: Jays' Anthony Santander stays quiet after team asks him to publicly address anti-Muslim social media posts
items.summary_auto: The Toronto Blue Jays have asked Anthony Santander to publicly address the controversy sparked by his decision to share anti-Muslim posts on social media. So far, the veteran outfielder has remained quiet and hasn't issued an apology.

items.title: Halifax’s Brian Ahern, who produced albums by Anne Murray and Johnny Cash, dead at 81
items.summary_auto: A Halifax-born music producer who played a big role in helping encourage fellow Bluenoser Anne Murray to pursue a career in music and later produced albums by artists such as Johnny Cash and Emmylou Harris is being remembered for the mark he left on the music industry.
